Lasso up This Dump-and-Bake Cowgirl Casserole for an Easy Dinner
4.0
(2)
1 Review

It’s spirited, sassy, and comes together in just 10 minutes.
By Sara Bir
Published on May 28, 2026

Baked casserole dish with a serving spoon and a plate of the dish served on the side
Credit:

Simply Recipes / Photo by Jen Causey / Food Styling by Margaret Monroe Dickey / Prop Styling by Julia Bayless

    Using frozen veggies means no chopping, so dinner comes together with little hands-on prep.
    Tex-Mex flavors gives this chicken and rice casserole a familiar profile with more zip.
    Rotisserie chicken, rich sauce, and fajita seasoning make each scoop hearty and bold.
    A quick broil browns the cheddar on top, giving the casserole a bubbly finish.

In the parade of stick-to-your-ribs recipes named after cowboys, this cowgirl casserole gives the ladies their due. A Tex-Mex inspired take on a chicken and rice casserole, it’s a welcome change of pace yet packed with familiar flavors. Best of all, thanks to frozen vegetables, there’s no chopping—just mix the ingredients and bake.
What Is Cowgirl Casserole?

Alas, cowgirl casserole is not an invention of Dale Evans or Pasty Montana, though I imagine they would both approve. Rice enriched with a rich sauce envelops bits of rotisserie chicken, while fajita seasoning provides a lively flavor. Serve with a simple green salad and sliced avocados to round out the meal.
A baked cowgirl casserole in a dish with a serving spoon accompanied by a plated portion

Simply Recipes / Photo by Jen Causey / Food Styling by Margaret Monroe Dickey / Prop Styling by Julia Bayless
Tips and Swaps for Cowgirl Casserole

    You can use leftover rice instead of pre-cooked rice. If you don’t have leftover rice, cook about 1 1/2 cups of dry rice, spread it out evenly on a rimmed baking sheet to cool down after cooking, then refrigerate it, uncovered, for 30 minutes until it’s cold and slightly dry on top. Fluff well to separate the grains before mixing into the casserole. 
    If you don’t have ground coriander, try cumin. The flavor will be slightly warmer and earthier.
    Turn it into a beef casserole by replacing the chicken with cooked, seasoned ground beef.
    Add a can of drained black beans or corn for even more heartiness.
    Cream of mushroom or cream of chicken soup can work in place of cream of onion soup. 

Make Ahead Cowgirl Casserole

To make cowgirl casserole ahead of time, assemble the casserole, cover with foil, and refrigerate for up to 24 hours before baking. Add an extra 5 to 10 minutes of baking time if you’re baking the casserole straight from the fridge. 

Cowgirl casserole freezes well. Bake the casserole, cool, then wrap tightly in a double layer of foil and freeze for up to 2 months. Thaw overnight in the refrigerator before reheating.
How to Freeze Lasagna and Other Casseroles
Baked casserole with melted cheese chicken rice and vegetables in a dish

Simply Recipes / Photo by Jen Causey / Food Styling by Margaret Monroe Dickey / Prop Styling by Julia Bayless

    Easy Chicken Enchilada Casserole

    Salsa Verde Chicken Bake
    Marry Me Chicken Casserole

Prep Time:
10 mins
Cook Time:
30 mins
Resting time:
15 mins
Total Time:
55 mins
Servings:
8 servings
Yield:
1 (9x13-inch) casserole
Note:

If you can’t find fire-roasted frozen vegetables, use an equal amount of regular frozen bell pepper and onion strips—you’ll miss out some smoky flavor, but the casserole will turn out just fine.

This recipe was developed by Renu Dhar.
Keep Screen Awake
Ingredients

    Nonstick cooking spray

    2 (8.8-ounce) packages precooked microwavable long-grain white rice (about 4 cups)

    1 (16-ounce) jar chunky salsa

    1 (14.4-ounce) bag frozen fire-roasted bell pepper and onion blend, thawed and drained

    1 (10.5-ounce) can cream of onion soup (such as Campbell’s)

    1 (1-ounce) package fajita seasoning mix

    1 teaspoon ground coriander

    1 teaspoon dried oregano

    1 1/2 cups (6 ounces) shredded sharp cheddar cheese, divided

    3 cups shredded cooked chicken

    1/4 cup chicken stock

Directions

    Preheat the oven to 375°F. 

    Lightly coat a broiler-safe 9x13-inch baking dish with nonstick cooking spray.
    Assemble the casserole:

    Add the rice, salsa, thawed bell pepper and onion blend, cream of onion soup, fajita seasoning,  coriander, oregano, and 1/2 cup of the cheese to the baking dish and stir until combined.

    Stir in the chicken until it’s evenly distributed, then stir in the broth. Sprinkle the remaining 1 cup of cheese on top. Cover the baking dish tightly with aluminum foil.
    Bake: 

    Bake, covered, until heated through and bubbling around edges, about 25 minutes.

    Remove the foil. Turn the oven to broil; broil until the cheese is lightly browned in spots, about 5 minutes.
    Rest and serve:

    Let the casserole stand for 15 minutes for the sauce to thicken before serving. 

    Refrigerate leftovers, tightly covered, for up to 4 days.

    Love the recipe? Leave us stars and a comment below!
